system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal, privileged. Do not send to the Seller.

**Headline:** The Seller's package moves against us on almost every point. Several positions in the Seller Update are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter: Bluefen is "addressed" yet no consent exists, and Riverlark is to be handled "post-completion" although the facility is unpaid. Two fallbacks the Seller has pre-empted (the 20% cap and the 18-month period) need Amelia Frost's written authority, and we have none. We should not concede them.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; once exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with a tipping basket.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours, and the deductible structure would strip out a large share of legitimate claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. Also, any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Hold at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The default wording also silently drags Fundamental, Tax and indemnity claims into the general limits (see SPA-N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties carry the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and a period of at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** Title and capacity go to the root of what we are buying, and a 20% cap on title to the very shares acquired is not acceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 and in the general limitations clause.** This is non-waivable under our playbook, and no one on the team may concede it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** DL [1.1]–[1.2] generally disclose the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Only specific disclosures, made fairly against particular warranties.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete [1.1] and [1.2]. Disclosures count only if specific and fair.** Whole-data-room and public-record disclosure would empty the warranties of content. Also resist [1.4]'s non-admission language to the extent it undercuts how the disclosures operate.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 bars any claim for matters known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must turn on named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** It operates as constructive buyer knowledge on top of general disclosure. If any version survives, it must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only; the condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence, before Completion, that its conditions are satisfied.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent (with its cl 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied) a non-waivable-by-Seller Condition Precedent.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m), so reasonable endeavours is too weak. Consent-on-delivery could also close us over an unsatisfied condition. Note that "addressed" in the Update is not borne out by the DL.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release to be provided after Completion. DL §3 confirms about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, unrepaid and undischarged.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** We need a payout letter, repayment from the funds flow and executed releases (including PPSR discharges) at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from the lender and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or otherwise Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require a funds-flow line item (or a price deduction / Debt treatment) for AUD 420,000 plus on-costs, backed by a specific indemnity.** These are Company obligations triggered by Completion. Leaving them off the funds flow shifts the cost to us.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering title, transfer and third-party IP claims relating to the Ironquay materials, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity.** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the Project Materials depend on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, and the data room has no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Also ask for a confirmatory assignment as a deliverable. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 in DD-010 as verified either way. Seek bank evidence or an Ironquay confirmation.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** Logs preserved, the investigation continued, and regular updates provided.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation.** Seek covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation (scope of about 1,240 records, access, NDB assessment) and give updates before Completion. Add a specific warranty or indemnity for any resulting regulatory or third-party cost. Neutral framing matters here. Nothing yet establishes a breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, so we should not assert one either.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment first, with no automatic classification either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Ask for the DD-008/DD-011 contracts and timing details** to determine whether each renewal is committed, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Reserve the position. Do not concede "ordinary course", and do not yet propose Debt classification or a price deduction.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 says any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise. Tax and IP are folded into the "general regime". Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment/funds-flow and covenant claims kept in their own categories, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reverse the default.** General limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims expressly identified as such. The Seller's drafting quietly caps every other category at 20% / 18 months.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL §10 concedes this is only the source relied on.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Require independent verification:**
  - an ASIC extract;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - share certificates and the constitution;
  - board approvals of the share issues and transfers;
  - Seller authority resolutions; and
  - an encumbrance release (linked to Riverlark).

  DD-012 is the Seller's own internal record, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms treated as open.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation.** Tax and IP should stay open for negotiation as separate categories (see SPA-N-014). We should not concede general-regime treatment or claim unlimited liability as our position. Neither has been agreed.

---

### Next steps
1. Send the mark-up holding all playbook starting positions. Do not deploy the 20% or 18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft.
2. Send information requests on:
   - Bluefen consent status and cl 11.3 conditions;
   - the Riverlark payout letter;
   - DD-005 on-costs;
   - Ironquay payment evidence;
   - the DD-006 investigation status; and
   - the Sandbar contracts.
3. Escalate SPA-N-005 (fraud) internally as a red line in case the Seller pushes back.
=== END ADVICE ===
